chunks: I asked him about the slaughter, so he said: 'When you slaughter, release it and do not restrain the forelimbs, and do not flip the knife so as to insert it from beneath the throat and cut upward. And releasing applies to birds in particular. So if it falls into a well or a hollow in the ground, do not eat it and do not feed it (to others), for you do not know whether the falling killed it or the slaughter.

And if it is from the sheep, then hold it by its wool or its hair, and do not hold a foreleg or a hind leg. As for cattle, hobble their legs and leave the tail free. As for camels, tie their hooves to their flanks and leave their hind legs free. And if something from the birds escapes you while you intend to slaughter it, or breaks free from you, shoot it with your arrow. And when it falls, purify it (slaughter it) in the manner of hunted game.

key_terms.الإِرْسَال: Releasing/letting hang — the prescribed position during slaughter where the animal is not fully restrained
key_terms.التَّرَدِّي: Falling into a pit — a cause of death that renders the slaughter uncertain and thus impermissible
key_terms.الذَّبْح: Islamic ritual slaughter — cutting the throat of a permissible animal in a prescribed manner
key_terms.الصَّيْد: Hunted game — the category under which an escaped and arrow-shot bird is classified
key_terms.الْحُلْقُوم: Windpipe/throat — the organ that must be cut during halal slaughter

ai.seo_question: What are the Islamic rulings on proper slaughter according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) provides detailed jurisprudential rulings on proper Islamic slaughter (dhabh). The Imam specifies that the animal must be released (not fully restrained) during slaughter, the knife must not be flipped to cut upward from below the windpipe, and different animals require different restraint methods: sheep by wool/hair (not limbs), cattle by hobbling the legs (tail free), and camels by tying hooves to flanks (hind legs free). If an animal falls into a pit after slaughter, it may not be eaten due to uncertainty whether the fall or slaughter caused death. If a bird escapes, it may be shot with an arrow and treated like game.
